Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: A small, 180 meter wide tornado would develop south-southwest of Klovborg. Initially an IF0-IF0.5, but quickly strengthened as it uprooted large trees and debranched several others. It tore whole roofs off of older homes and farms. It toppled gravestones and ripped some tiles off of a church. One of Denmark's oldest open-gardens was completely destroyed, with greenhouses damaged, large swaths of trees uprooted, snapped, or debranched.

A video from a Facebook group (TV2 Vejret Billeder) shows what might be, either a wedge, or a rainwrapped tornado over Jels, and damage was reported in the town of Jels which is the direction the video was filmed.

Another long-tracked F3 tornado began near Howard, Georgia, striking the communities Roberta, Knoxville, Lizella, Vineville and Macon, damaging or destroying over 750 homes, killing five, and injuring 75.
An F1 satellite tornado was also observed northeast of Butler, damaging or destroying homes, but causing no casualties.

Another weak, but fatal, long-tracked F1 tornado developed near Reynolds, moving through rural areas before striking Byron, Centerville and Elberta on the north side of Warner Robins and Robins Air Force Base. It then impacted Bullard east of there before dissipating. The tornado produced moderate to heavy damage along its path, especially in Elberta, where it unroofed or destroyed 12 small homes and killed a tenant farmer. Five other people were injured (Grazulis rated the tornado F2).

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: Later, further to the south in Illinois, a deadly, long‐tracked F3 tornado touched down near Saunemin and moved northeastward, lifting briefly before touching down again in Limestone Township. Continuing northeastward, the tornado tore through Indian Oaks north of Kankakee as a bell‐shaped funnel cloud, destroying most of the town before ending west of Grant Park. Eight homes and 30 other buildings were destroyed, 30 other homes and 46 other buildings were damaged, about 30 farms lost buildings, and empty storage tanks were rolled for over 1 mile (1.6 km).

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: The final strong tornado of outbreak was a brief F2 tornado in Swartz Creek, Michigan that was described as 'seven fingers dangling beneath a dark cloud' with one of them touching down. That afternoon, a large, long-tracked, violent 550 yd (500 m) wide F4 tornado plowed through Marion, Knighthood Village, Harrisburg, Huber, Waterloo, and Boston, Indiana as well as West Florence and Eaton, Ohio, injuring seven on its 63.1 mi (101.5 km) path.

Another F2 tornado then injured two southeast of Clarksville, Tennessee.
Limited tornado activity occurred over the next four days with an F2 tornado injuring two in Spring Hill, Alabama on April 27.

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: It started when the strongest tornado of the year touched down and became a large, 800 yd (730 m) wide F5 storm as it tore through northern Tecumseh, eastern Shawnee (both of which had been hit by a long‐tracked F3 tornado or tornado family earlier in the day), Prague, southeastern Kellyville, and Sapulpa, killing five and injuring 81 along its long 71.8 miles (115.6 km) track.[61][62]
Later, a short-lived, but strong F3 tornado struck Hoffman, killing two and injuring 15.[63]

Later, another long-tracked, violent F4 tornado became the deadliest of the outbreak when it struck Wilburton, western McCurtain, Keota, and southwestern Sallisaw, killing 16 and injuring 106 on its 62.4 miles (100.4 km) path.[64]
At the same time, a destructive F2 tornado hit Texanna and eastern Duchess Landing, killing two and injuring six.[65]
An F3 tornado struck western Moffett and western West Fort Smith, killing one.[66]
A violent F4 tornado then ripped through Roland and Remy, killing five and injuring 13.[67]
The final Oklahoma tornado of the outbreak was an F3 twister that blew through Bokoshe, Gans, and Akins, killing one.[68]
Early the next morning in Arkansas, a deadly F3 tornado struck Menifee, Wooster, Greenbrier, and southern Enders, killing one and injuring 30.[69]

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: The tornado touched down in southeastern Houston to the east of Brookside Village in El Franco Lee Park and caused minor damage to several homes, trees, and fences.[1][9]
It then strengthened and struck the Beamer Place Apartments at EF2 intensity.[1][9]
The nearby Beverly Hills Intermediate School and Challenger Intermediate School were also damaged at EF2 intensity.[9]

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Num: several apartment buildings, businesses, homes, and Genoa Elementary School
Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: As the tornado crossed I-45, it caused mainly mid-range EF1 damage to several apartment buildings, businesses, homes, and Genoa Elementary School as it entered the Genoa neighborhood.[9]
A small pocket of high-end EF2 damage occurred in this area as a metal building was destroyed.[9]
The tornado caused high-end-EF1 to low-end EF2 damage as it entered the southeastern part of Pasadena and moved through Burke Crenshaw Park, where most of a building's roof was blown off.[9]

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Num: Pasadena Memorial High School, several businesses, and many homes
Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: Continuing through Pasadena, the tornado struck Pasadena Memorial High School, several businesses, and many homes at EF1 intensity, causing considerable roof damage.[9]

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Num: Some homes had their roofs torn off, a few had exterior walls removed, one home was mostly destroyed
Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: After crossing Beltway 8, the tornado entered a subdivision near Bliss Meadows Park and caused significant damage to homes—some roofs were torn off, exterior walls removed, and one home was mostly destroyed (rated EF2).[9]

Locations: eastern part of the Golden Acres neighborhood
Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Num: homes were severely damaged, and a church was largely destroyed
Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: After briefly weakening, more EF2 damage occurred in the eastern part of the Golden Acres neighborhood, where homes were severely damaged and a church was largely destroyed.[9]

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Num: many homes damaged, with a few having large portions of roofs removed
Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: After crossing Red Bluff Road, the tornado produced EF0 to EF1 damage, downing trees and damaging the roofs of many homes in residential areas, with some having large portions removed.[9]
In Deer Park, a Walgreens, Deer Park Public Library, and St. Hyacinth Catholic Church were heavily damaged at EF2 intensity.[1][9]
The San Jacinto Manor nursing home suffered major structural damage, including partial collapse of its roof and walls.[10][11]

Locations: E X Street and Luella Avenue
Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: A single home at the corner of E X Street and Luella Avenue in Deer Park had its whole roof and several walls removed at EF2 intensity.[1][9]
As the tornado crossed SH 225, it produced widespread high-end EF0 to EF1 damage, with many homes sustaining damage to their roofs and garages.

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Num: several mobile homes damaged or destroyed, and some houses shifted off their foundations
Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: After reaching EF3 intensity, the tornado crossed Houston Ship Channel into the Wooster section of Baytown at high-end EF1 strength, damaging several mobile homes and shifting some houses off their foundations.[1][9]
After leaving Baytown, the tornado further weakened to EF0 intensity, causing minor damage to power lines and some industrial building near I-10 before lifting.[9][1]

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: An EF2 tornado hit the town of Baring, Missouri on the night of August 4, causing extensive damage to homes, businesses, and other structures and injuring two people.

A long-tracked EF2 tornado touched down north of Pawnee, Illinois in Sangamon County two days later, damaging or destroying homes and causing extensive tree damage as it passed near Kincaid and Taylorville before it dissipated near Assumption in Christian County, almost an hour after touching down.
Later that night, three simultaneous tornadoes (one rated EF0 and two rated EF1) caused considerable damage in and around Paoli, Indiana.
On August 7, a high-end EF2 tornado hit the west side of Knoxville, Tennessee, badly damaging some homes and an apartment complex.
A low-end EF3 tornado moved through southern Lewis County, New York, striking the town of Turin and causing significant damage at the Snow Ridge Ski Resort at the end of its 16-mile (26 km) path.

On August 8, multiple storm chasers documented a highly-visible EF3 stovepipe tornado that looped over its path multiple times outside of Yuma, Colorado, destroying well-built farm buildings and equipment, snapping large power poles, and severely damaging a house in rural Yuma County.

It strengthened as it hit the neighboring town of Nusbaum, where well-built masonry homes and buildings had their roofs torn off, a few outbuildings were destroyed, and large trees were snapped.
